title: The Agreement on the Realignment of the Boundary between the Jakarta and the Singapore Flight Information Regions
what_it_is: The Agreement on the Realignment of the Boundary between the Jakarta and the Singapore Flight Information Regions

sections.label: Jakarta-Singapore FIR boundary realignment
sections.summary: The Jakarta and Singapore FIR boundary will be realigned to meet Indonesia's desire and reflect its territorial baselines, with Indonesia delegating airspace closest to Changi to Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: The boundary between the Jakarta FIR and the Singapore FIR will be realigned to meet Indonesia's desire to realign the FIR boundaries, and largely take into account Indonesia's territorial baselines.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: Indonesia will delegate to Singapore the provision of ANS for the airspace closest to Changi, to meet Changi Airport's current and future needs.

sections.label: 25-year FIR delegation arrangement
sections.summary: The FIR Agreement's delegation arrangement lasts 25 years and shall be extended by mutual consent if both sides find it beneficial.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: Fourth, the delegation arrangement under the FIR Agreement is for 25 years and shall be extended by mutual consent if both sides find it beneficial to do so.

sections.label: FIR Agreement resolves longstanding issue
sections.summary: The FIR Agreement resolves a key longstanding bilateral issue and paves the way for closer air traffic management and aviation cooperation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: The FIR Agreement decisively resolves a key longstanding issue on the bilateral agenda and paves the way for closer cooperation in air traffic management and other aviation issues.

sections.label: Singapore continues providing ANS
sections.summary: The FIR Agreement lets Singapore continue providing ANS within a contiguous airspace block sufficient for Changi Airport's present and future needs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: The FIR Agreement allows Singapore to continue providing ANS within a contiguous block of airspace which is sufficient for Changi Airport's present and future needs.

sections.label: Coordination procedures and ICAO proposal
sections.summary: Technical teams are working through detailed coordination procedures, and Singapore and Indonesia will jointly consult stakeholders and submit a Proposal for Amendment to ICAO.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: Second, the technical teams are working through the detailed coordination procedures for the FIR Agreement, which are necessary to ensure a smooth transition in air navigation arrangements and to uphold safety and efficiency.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: Third, Singapore and Indonesia will jointly consult all relevant stakeholders and submit a Proposal for Amendment for the FIR boundary realignment and delegation arrangement to ICAO for approval.

sections.label: Delegation arrangement extension by consent
sections.summary: Under the FIR Agreement, the delegation arrangement shall be extended by mutual consent should both sides find it beneficial.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: Under the FIR Agreement, the delegation arrangement shall be extended by mutual consent, should both sides find it beneficial to do so.

sections.label: 25-year agreements and disputes
sections.summary: Both the DCA and FIR Agreement last 25 years, with disputes settled by consultation, and existing arrangements continue until a new agreement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: Each of the agreements lasts for 25 years – the DCA and the FIR Agreement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: If there are disputes, both sides will consult and reach an amicable settlement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: What happens after 25 years is that the existing arrangements will continue until we reach a new agreement.

sections.label: Three agreements brought into force
sections.summary: The agreement between both countries is to bring all three agreements into force simultaneously.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: The agreement between both countries is to bring into force all three agreements simultaneously.

sections.label: FIR delegation arrangement extension
sections.summary: The FIR Agreement delegation arrangement lasts 25 years and may be extended by mutual consent, with Indonesia, Singapore and ICAO consulting before the end.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: If I may reiterate, the delegation arrangement under the FIR Agreement is for 25 years and it also states that it shall be extended by mutual consent if both sides find it beneficial to do so.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Indonesia and Singapore will consult each other and ICAO prior to the end of 25 years to ensure safety and efficiency of international civil aviation beyond the 25 years.

sections.label: Assurance for Changi Airport hub
sections.summary: Without that assurance, it is difficult to move forward for Changi Airport and Singapore as an international aviation hub needing safe landings and take-offs.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Without that assurance, it is really difficult to contemplate how we can move forward for Changi Airport and Singapore, because, ultimately, we are an international aviation hub and, central to that, is our ability to ensure the aircraft landings and take-offs in Changi Airport can be done safely and efficiently.

sections.label: Agreement gives clarity and confidence
sections.summary: The agreement gives clarity, certainty and confidence to move forward on many issues for Changi Airport, bilateral aviation cooperation and serving international aviation.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: This, again, is going to be an important part of the work going forward.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: So, if I may go back to what I said in response to an earlier question, whilst the details will evolve as we see the situation developing, the key thing is that this agreement, at its foundation, gives us the clarity, certainty and confidence to move forward on many issues, not just in the interest of Changi Airport, but also in our bilateral interests in terms of aviation cooperation and how we can better serve the international aviation community as air travel grows in Asia.

sections.label: Shared commitment to aviation safety
sections.summary: Both sides had a shared commitment to ensuring the safety and efficiency of international civil aviation, which helped reach this outcome.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: One of the reasons we were able to get to this outcome is because both sides had a shared commitment to ensuring the safety and efficiency of international civil aviation.

sections.label: Consultative process on aviation outcome
sections.summary: A consultative process over an extended period produced an outcome believed good for Indonesia, Singapore and international civil aviation.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: That is what this process has been about.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: It has been a consultative process, there have been discussions over an extended period and we have now arrived at an outcome that we believe is good for Indonesia, Singapore and international civil aviation.

sections.label: Agreement, ratification and air navigation partnerships
sections.summary: An agreement exists today, and the priority is ratification and entry into force, with no option precluded for air navigation services partnerships.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: I would say we have an agreement today.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: I think the first and most important thing is for us to make sure they are ratified and they enter into force.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: As I pointed out in my Ministerial Statement, there are all kinds of partnerships in the provision of air navigation services around the world.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: So, I would not preclude any option going forward, but the basis for ideas like what the Member has suggested, really is that it must be premised on first having a close understanding and cooperation between all the parties concerned and this must be borne out by experience that it can work to mutual benefit and accommodate the needs of both sides well.
